text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Friday morning newspapers:
- Premier Janez Drnovsek said he would seek a vote of confidence if Slovenia failed to be included in the first round of EU expansion even after approving an accord with the bloc.
- Parliament passed a new law determining minimum wages on Thursday. According to the new law, salaries will be adjusted to the rise of consumer price inflation once a year.
- Number of unemployed Slovenians in May fell one percent to 122,518, compared to April and rose 3.5 percent from May 1996, the country's employment office said.
- Strike of employees of commercial television station TV3, pushing for payment of salaries for the last six months, will continue until their demands are met, strikers said.

- Slovenian non-governmental organisations protested against the government's announcement that it will cancel a refugee status to 2,000 out of 7,000 Bosnian refugees in Slovenia from the end of next month.
- Number of newly registered cars in April rose to 8,721, an increase of almost a third compared to the same month last year.
- Government on Thursday adopted a draft budget for the first nine months of 1997, setting government spending at 532.1 billion tolars ($3.4 billion) and income at 505.4 billion.
